Recent findings suggest that we've seen the GTA VI Easter eggs, we've admired the best GTA VI brand reactions and we've dived into the history of the Grand Theft Auto logo. Today, let's turn our attention to the artists.

I don't mean the artists who made the game – we've already interviewed Rockstar Games' art team about GTA VI's environmental storytelling and the building design in GTA VI. I mean the players who are turning their passion for the game into art of their own.

I hesitate to say "turning GTA VI into art" because it already is art. But there are players who are using the game's vast world as a creative medium for their own expression, whether through in-game virtual photography or capturing scenes from the game in other media.

There's nowhere near enough space here to mention all of the people who are making art from the game, but here are just a few examples.

A post shared by Photoingame (@photo.in.game).

GTA VI's Photo Studio, available from the pause menu, provides adjustable camera settings such as aspect ratio, aperture, and depth of field and lighting controls for in-game virtual photography.

Industry observers note that players can frame shots, hunt for the perfect lighting, compose scenes, and capture images that resemble fashion, street, documentary or landscape photography. Photo Studio even has filters and post-processing effects, so you don't need to take your shots into the best photo editing software like Photoshop.

The dedicated PlayStation in-game artist Photo.in.game (above) shows that creating art in photo mode is about much more than taking a simple screenshot, demonstrating their editing process for a shot of Jason and Lucia at sunset.

A post shared by cone^ (@theconestudio).

The Cone Studio has been sharing multiple daily shots from GTA VI taken not with the in-game Photo Studio but with a real-world Sony Alpha Nex 5n. Using a low shutter speed and some curves and hue filters in post, they're creating some evocative shots that feel drenched in nostalgia.

A post shared by Fons ᵈᵉ Haan (@f0nzel).

There are phones in GTA VI, and phones can shoot hyperlapses. So Fons de Haan has done just that: a hyperlapse made only using Jason's in-game phone.

A post shared by Kindred Cameras (@kindredcameras).

Australia-based Kindred Cameras (above) has been bringing in-game shots of the GTA VI's stunning environments into the real world by printing them as Polaroids. Anyone unfamiliar with the game might never connect this piece of art to a controversially violent game franchise.

I made an oil painting of Jason stealing a mobility scooter in GTA VI https://t.co/ei0axkXs72November 25, 2026.

The artist Cayde (above) is painting scenes from GTA using oil paints. Again, the use of physical media brings the game into the real world. His subjects so far have included Jason stealing a mobility scooter and Cal and Jason snuggling. He's been painting some scenes live on Twitch. Check out his website.

GTA VI is an incredible achievement that sets a new bar for game graphics, and it also has a very distinct aesthetic, so it's perhaps only natural that it would inspire players to create their own art.

According to recent reports, as I stated, this is just a sample of how people are finding inspiration int the game. There's also the traditional fan art, design and brand concepts, which perhaps deserve a post all of their own. Let me know in the comments if you've spotted some more good examples.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Order builds the Sonny's Corner brand identity from a hand-lettered subway poster alphabet, one deep red, and a diamond that holds it together.
  • The bar sits on the corner of Greenpoint Avenue and Franklin Street in Brooklyn, at 142 Franklin Street, on a spot that has served the neighborhood as a bar for almost a hundred years.
  • Industry observers note that the typeface is the whole idea.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Order builds the Sonny's Corner brand identity from a hand-lettered subway poster alphabet, one deep red, and a diamond that holds it together.

The bar sits on the corner of Greenpoint Avenue and Franklin Street in Brooklyn, at 142 Franklin Street, on a spot that has served the neighborhood as a bar for almost a hundred years. Its previous tenant was the Pencil Factory, named after the Eberhard-Faber Pencil Factory across the street, and Order lets that history set the tone without turning it into costume. The name does double work. Sonny is one owner's newborn child, and the corner itself catches the best afternoon light in the neighborhood. The lockup indicates it plainly: a white diamond on a deep red field, the name set in chunky hand-drawn capitals that feel painted rather than typed.

Industry observers note that the typeface is the whole idea. Order worked with Brooklyn type designer Ben Tuttle on Oppy Sans, a revival of the hand lettering Amelia Opdyke Jones drew for The Subway Sun, the New York subway etiquette posters that ran from 1918 to around 1965. Jones signed the posters as Oppy, and her letters carry the jokes and the warnings in the same loose hand. The revival keeps that hand-drawn character, and Order runs the single style everywhere: identification, signage, packaging, and everything between. One style, no supporting cast, so the voice never wavers. The specimen highlights the full alphabet with numerals and punctuation, and the letters hold their shape from a matchbook up to the shopfront.

In a recent development, the color comes from the room itself. A deep red was chosen to match the wooden interior and the seating upholstery, and simple neutrals carry the rest. The diamond from the lockup repeats as a harlequin pattern across the matchbooks, the coasters, and the awning over the door. The same red runs through the pens, the caps, the tote bag, and the business cards, each one carrying the name small and straight. The motto on the window reads Where the sun always shines, a line that works three ways at once: the child, the typeface, and the corner itself, which lines up with Manhattan's 23rd Street corridor and catches the afternoon sun. If you know, you know.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Rather than concealing the solar plates beneath the dial, the watch reveals them through a precisely cut circular opening, turning a functional component into a defining visual feature.
  • The design builds on the distinctive visual language of Mondaine‘s Doppio collection, which is characterised by double-line hands and indexes, a concave dial and a double-domed sapphire crystal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Swiss watchmaker Mondaine has expanded its Doppio collection with the Solar Skeleton, a timepiece that brings solar technology into the foreground of its design.

Rather than concealing the solar plates beneath the dial, the watch reveals them through a precisely cut circular opening, turning a functional component into a defining visual feature.

The design builds on the distinctive visual language of Mondaine‘s Doppio collection, which is characterised by double-line hands and indexes, a concave dial and a double-domed sapphire crystal.

Mondaine explained that these elements establish a sense of repetition, rhythm and structural clarity, while the exposed solar plates introduce an additional layer of depth and visual interest.

While solar technology is typically hidden from view, Mondaine has taken a different approach with the Doppio Solar Skeleton.

A carefully positioned circular opening around the centre of the dial offers a controlled view of the solar movement, while the outer section retains the indexes to ensure clear readability.

By making the technology visible, Mondaine aimed to bridge the watch’s technical function with its aesthetic identity, without compromising the “clarity and legibility” that define the collection.

Powered by a Swiss Ronda solar movement, the watch converts natural and artificial light into electrical energy, which is stored in a rechargeable battery.

According to Mondaine, a few minutes of sunlight can reactivate a fully discharged movement, while a full charge provides a power reserve of up to eight months in complete darkness.

The brand explained that this technology eliminates the need for regular battery replacements, offering a more resource-conscious approach to timekeeping.

The Doppio Solar Skeleton is available in two versions, each offering a different interpretation of its distinctive design.

The first combines a polished silver 316L stainless steel case with a vegan grape leather strap, bringing together traditional watchmaking materials and a contemporary material alternative.

The second features a polished black stainless steel case paired with a matching mesh bracelet, creating a more monochromatic appearance that emphasises the watch’s clean lines and geometric detailing.

Both versions feature a 41-millimetre case, a discreet date window and a precisely laser-etched Mondaine logo and solar markings.

A double-domed sapphire crystal and water resistance of up to 5 ATM complete the design, “combining refined aesthetics with everyday practicality”.

“With the Doppio Solar Skeleton, we wanted to make solar technology part of the design itself,” stated Mondaine.

“By revealing the cells beneath the dial, we have created a watch where functionality becomes a defining aesthetic feature, while staying true to Mondaine’s principles of clarity, precision and Swiss design.”.

The Doppio Solar Skeleton reflects Mondaine’s commitment to iconic Swiss minimalist design, where form and function work together.

By integrating visible solar technology into the collection’s established design language, the watch intends to demonstrate how a functional element can become an integral part of a timepiece’s aesthetic identity.

To find out more about Mondaine and the Doppio Solar Skeleton, visit the brand’s website.

10 Signs You Might Not Really Be in Love: How to Tell the Difference

📅 26 Jun 2024 | ⏱️ 3 min read (689 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Greatist

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Love can feel like navigating a choose-your-own-adventure book with half the pages missing.
  • According to recent reports, wondering how to tell the difference?
  • Feeling a bit puzzled about your feelings for boo?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Love can feel like navigating a choose-your-own-adventure book with half the pages missing. Are you truly in love or just caught in a wave of infatuation? Sometimes, what seems like a heart-thumping romance may be a fleeting crush.

According to recent reports, wondering how to tell the difference? We’ve got you! Here’s a rundown of the 10 signs you’re not really in love.

Feeling a bit puzzled about your feelings for boo? That’s pretty normal. But before you start planning your future or picking out matching Halloween costumes, you may wanna make sure it’s real love and not a case of a serious crush.

Here are some signs that you may not really be in love:.

Sources indicate that caught up in the romance novel vibe? If you’re all about the feelings of being in love rather than who’s sharing your popcorn, it might just be that you’re smitten with the idea of love itself.

Time to check if your relationship is more about the fairy tale than the real person.

Chatting with your partner shouldn’t feel as shallow as a kiddie pool. If deep talks are tougher than pulling teeth and rarer than a unicorn, it’s a red flag.

Sticking to small talk about the weather and dinner plans suggests the emotional depth for a lasting bond might be missing.

When discussions about future prepares feel as far-fetched as sci-fi adventures, they may reveal underlying doubts about the relationship’s viability.

If imagining a future together feels unrealistic or undesirable, it’s time to ask yourself why. Real love looks a future; infatuation lives for the weekend.

Remember when their sock on the floor was cute? If little quirks now make you more cranky than charmed, it might mean the love goggles are off, your feelings have shifted from affection to annoyance, and the reality check has bounced.

Love is seeing imperfections and adoring them anyway.

Feeling more at ease or more ‘yourself’ when your partner isn’t around is a telling sign. If you’re secretly throwing mini-parties when they leave the room, you need to stop and think. Real-deal love means missing their chaos when they’re gone, not celebrating the silence.

Industry observers note that shared values are the anchor of deep, lasting relationships. If your core values clash more than a polka dot and stripes ensemble, you’re in for a rough ride, as finding common ground could be challenging!

Lasting love grows from shared beliefs and mutual respect, not from opposing battle lines.

No respect? No future. Respect is as critical to love as air is to breathing. Without mutual respect, you might just be coexisting rather than genuinely connecting.

If you no longer admire or respect each other’s opinions and choices, sustaining a healthy relationship will be difficult.

If they’re out of sight and totally out of mind, that’s not just independence — it might be indifference. When love is real, you should long for their laugh or lame jokes when they’re away. Could it be that your emotional attachment isn’t as strong as it should be for a lasting relationship?

If your best moments are consistently away from your partner, your heart might not be in it to win it. Perhaps your relationship isn’t providing enough support or happiness.

It has been revealed that true love enriches your life and doesn’t play second fiddle to your social circle. It’s time to evaluate where your emotional energy is invested.

Still window shopping while you’re supposedly locked down? It’s a sign you might not be all in. A love that lasts doesn’t keep a backup catalog — it’s too busy loving what it already has.

Knowing why you’re still scanning for alternatives can help you address what might be missing or unfulfilled in your relationship.

Are you genuinely in love or just in love with being in love? If you’re secretly thrilled when they’re not around, stuck in surface-level chit-chat, or dreading deep-future talks, these are cosmic signs that it’s rethink o’clock.

Don’t ignore the signals — tuning in now can save you heartache later and lead you toward a love that genuinely fulfills you.
